target_statement: Calibrate the repository's template-quotient method against bases with known Lychrel numbers and supply a base-generic formal certificate theorem. (1) For every base b>=2, words Q(B,C,g) = B (b-1)^g C (b-1)^g rev(B) (least significant first; canonical exterior block B, symmetric center C, neutral band coefficient b-1): Lean proof of the exact one-step actual reverse-and-add transition while the two band carries differ, and of a conditional existence theorem: a finite interface cycle with nonnegative total gap gain and step safety yields an explicit base-b integer whose ordinary reverse-and-add orbit never reaches a palindrome. (2) Kernel-checked certificate instances in bases 2, 4, 8, 16 (exploratory Python finds period 2m+2, gap gain 1 cycles exactly in bases 2^m among b<=26 at small interface caps), with explicit seeds, e.g. 22 = 10110 in base 2. These are base-2^m results, explicitly NOT decimal and NOT about 196; known in the literature, so no novelty claim. (3) Decimal (b=10): exhaustive finite-scope searches of the same quotient at increasing interface caps, retained with UNKNOWN beyond caps; investigate an all-parameter decimal obstruction for the neutral one-band template (WIP, no claim until proved). (4) Exploratory calibration on bases 11, 17, 20, 26 (literature Lychrel bases): whether any template quotient in the repository's families exhibits their known mechanisms. No native_decide, no sorry/new axioms; core Lean 4.19.0 + Std.
